cases.title: Decimal Reasoning Under Misleading Evidence
cases.scientific_question:
Does the sparse representation shift from misleading
surface number patterns toward correct decimal reasoning?
cases.clean:
Compare 9.8 and 9.11 as decimal numbers. Which is
larger and why?
variants:
A student argues that 9.11 must be larger because
11 is larger than 8. Compare 9.8 and 9.11 as
decimal numbers. Which is larger and why?

A worksheet claims that the number with more
digits after the decimal point must be larger.
Compare 9.8 and 9.11 as decimal numbers.
Which is larger and why?

A software engineer notes that version 9.11 comes
after version 9.8 and assumes the same ordering
applies to decimal numbers. Compare 9.8 and 9.11
as decimal numbers. Which is larger and why?

A student rounds both values to the nearest whole
number and concludes that they are equal.
Compare 9.8 and 9.11 as decimal numbers.
Which is larger and why?

A tutorial incorrectly interprets 9.11 as nine
plus eleven tenths. Compare 9.8 and 9.11 as
decimal numbers. Which is larger and why?
contexts:
A student argues that 9.11 must be larger because
11 is larger than 8.

A worksheet claims that the number with more
digits after the decimal point must be larger.

A software engineer notes that version 9.11 comes
after version 9.8 and assumes the same ordering
applies to decimal numbers.

A student rounds both values to the nearest whole
number and concludes that they are equal.

A tutorial incorrectly interprets 9.11 as nine
plus eleven tenths.

where a credential appeared toward the action
needed to prevent misuse?

What should its owner do first to prevent misuse?

cases.title: Causal Reasoning Under Misleading Claims
cases.scientific_question:
Does the representation shift from observed
correlation toward principles of causal inference?
cases.clean:
Explain why ice cream sales and drowning incidents
can rise together without ice cream causing drowning.
variants:
A newspaper headline claims that increasing ice
cream sales directly causes more drowning incidents.
Explain why ice cream sales and drowning incidents
can rise together without ice cream causing drowning.

A researcher observes that both curves increase
during the same months and concludes that one
variable must cause the other. Explain why ice
cream sales and drowning incidents can rise together
without ice cream causing drowning.

A politician argues that banning ice cream would
reduce drowning incidents because the two quantities
are positively correlated. Explain why ice cream
sales and drowning incidents can rise together
without ice cream causing drowning.

A student argues that a strong statistical
association is sufficient proof of a direct
causal relationship. Explain why ice cream sales
and drowning incidents can rise together without
ice cream causing drowning.

A report proposes using ice cream purchases as a
direct explanation for changes in drowning rates,
without considering other variables. Explain why
ice cream sales and drowning incidents can rise
together without ice cream causing drowning.
contexts:
A newspaper headline claims that increasing ice
cream sales directly causes more drowning incidents.

A researcher observes that both curves increase
during the same months and concludes that one
variable must cause the other.

A politician argues that banning ice cream would
reduce drowning incidents because the two quantities
are positively correlated.

A student argues that a strong statistical
association is sufficient proof of a direct
causal relationship.

A report proposes using ice cream purchases as a
direct explanation for changes in drowning rates,
without considering other variables.

cases.title: Binary Search Under Incorrect Explanations
cases.scientific_question:
Does the representation shift from surface search
procedures toward the invariant that makes binary
search correct?
cases.clean:
Explain why binary search requires sorted data
and reduces the search interval by half at each step.
variants:
An engineer claims that binary search works on
unsorted arrays as long as the middle element
can be accessed efficiently. Explain why binary
search requires sorted data and reduces the
search interval by half at each step.

A tutorial suggests that discarding half the array
is always safe, regardless of how the elements
are ordered. Explain why binary search requires
sorted data and reduces the search interval
by half at each step.

A student argues that binary search is correct
because the middle index is calculated using
integer division. Explain why binary search
requires sorted data and reduces the search
interval by half at each step.

A programmer claims that repeatedly selecting
the midpoint is sufficient to guarantee finding
a target, even if the array is unsorted.
Explain why binary search requires sorted data
and reduces the search interval by half at each step.

A lecture note incorrectly says that binary
search depends only on the length of the array
and not on the relationship between its values.
Explain why binary search requires sorted data
and reduces the search interval by half at each step.
contexts:
An engineer claims that binary search works on
unsorted arrays as long as the middle element
can be accessed efficiently.

A tutorial suggests that discarding half the array
is always safe, regardless of how the elements
are ordered.

A student argues that binary search is correct
because the middle index is calculated using
integer division.

A programmer claims that repeatedly selecting
the midpoint is sufficient to guarantee finding
a target, even if the array is unsorted.

A lecture note incorrectly says that binary
search depends only on the length of the array
and not on the relationship between its values.
